subject: Embedded solution partner — revenue matrix, registration runbook
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Tiledeck Partnerships <partners@tiledeck.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Partnership commercial ask + lead registration process

Hi Priya / Tiledeck team,

Nice to meet you (virtually) — thanks for the product demo last week. We left excited about embedding Tiledeck’s analytics into our onboarding flow for a joint go-to-market bundle. Before we pull legal in, can you confirm two practical items so we can build internal forecasts:

1) A sample revenue-share matrix (gross revenue split by license / services / integration fee) — we want a 0/90/10 sense for low/expected/high adoption scenarios.
2) Your lead registration process and what evidence you require (SAO, signed SOW, opportunity ID) to protect referral/registration credit.

Can you also attach any standard MOU you use for ISV integrations? If you prefer, we can share a short revshare model and registration template we use to speed review.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Camila and Marissa from partner ops so they can align on on-boarding and attribution.

Best,

Dylan Brooks
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: revshare_model.xlsx (preview)

From: Priya Rao <priya@tiledeck.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tiledeck Partnerships <partners@tiledeck.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partnership commercial ask + lead registration process

Hi Dylan / Camila / Marissa,

Great to connect — we appreciate the clear ask. Attaching our standard MOU (Tiledeck_MOU_v1.docx) and a sample lead registration PDF. High-level answers below:

- Revenue splits: Our baseline for embedded ISV bundles is 70/30 (partner/integration owner) on software ARR for net-new customers, with a 50/50 split on professional services unless separately contracted. We typically provide a tiered uplift (to 75/25) once ARR contribution from the partner exceeds $200k ARR annually.
- Lead registration: We require the HubSpot opportunity ID, a short statement of qualification (BANT-style), and a signed mutual MOU for any deals > $50k ARR. For inbound or small pilot deals (< $50k) we accept a lead registration form plus email trail.

Questions for you: do you need exclusivity by vertical or territory? Also, are you able to accept quarter-delay payout terms for first 2 quarters while we validate usage?

Best,
Priya Rao
Head of Partnerships, Tiledeck
Attachments: Tiledeck_MOU_v1.docx, lead_reg_form.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@tiledeck.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Partnership commercial ask + lead registration process

Folks — forwarding Tiledeck’s reply and MOU. High level asks from partner: baseline 70/30 revshare, tiered uplift, lead registration tied to HubSpot opp ID, and request for short delayed payout for initial quarters.

Proposed internal approach (quick bullets):
- Option A (standard): Redwood pays partner 30% of software ARR on net-new customers attributed via registration form + HubSpot opp. Payout monthly with 30-day settlement.
- Option B (venture-safe): For first 2 quarters, payout follows quarter-delay (Tiledeck receives accrual report and payment at end of quarter+1). After $200k ARR contribution, uplift to 25% partner share retroactive to quarter start.
- Registration runbook: require HubSpot opp ID + signed MOU for deals >= $50k ARR. For pilot/POC under $50k, partner can submit lead_reg_form.pdf with initial evidence (customer email + discovery notes).

Ask: Camila / Marissa — can you validate that Option B is operationally feasible? Ben / Karthik — can you confirm the finance and legal implications (clawbacks, refunds, tax withholding) and estimate the payout cadence impact on cash flow? If OK, I’ll propose we send a short, single-page amendment to attach to Tiledeck_MOU_v1 and get DocuSign going.

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@tiledeck.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 15:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partnership commercial ask + lead registration process

Thanks — quick ops check and next steps:

- Ops: Option B is fine but we’ll need a machine-readable registration record (HubSpot opp + custom property "Partner Registered By") to avoid manual disputes. Marissa, can you add the partner property and a validation webhook?
- Finance: Ben flagged that quarter-delay payouts require an accrual template; asks for revshare_model.xlsx breakdown by ARR cohort and sample payments schedule. Ben: can you confirm whether Redwood can do monthly accruals and a single quarterly disbursement to Tiledeck?
- Legal: Karthik suggested a short amendment (1 page) that adds registration evidence, payout cadence, and uplift triggers. He asked to include a 12-month clawback window for refunds/cancellations.

Action items:
1) Marissa to create the HubSpot property and webhook — due 2026-12-10.
2) Ben to populate revshare_model.xlsx with cashflow impact and sample payment runs — due 2026-12-08.
3) Karthik to draft amendment language for the MOU and upload to Drive — due 2026-12-07.
4) Dylan to prepare the single-page amendment and DocuSign envelope for Tiledeck if internal sign-offs align — target send 2026-12-09.

Priya — we’ll share the amendment draft once Karthik has uploaded it and Ben has completed the model. Quick note: no exclusivity requested from Redwood at this stage.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Senior Partner Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
